newsitem.title: UK: Air Foyle eyes converted Airbus freighter lease.
newsitem.headline: Air Foyle eyes converted Airbus freighter lease.

text.p: UK independent cargo specialist Air Foyle may soon lease its first Airbus A300B4-200 converted freighter, chairman Chris Foyle said on Thursday.
"I am currently talking to a potential customer, who would contract us to fly the aircraft initially for three years," he told Reuters in an interview.
He declined to name the company concerned but said it was not TNT, with which Air Foyle already has a contract to fly BAe 146 freighters on overnight European express services
He said if the deal were concluded, the A300B4-200F would be based in Europe and would mainly operate cargo flights within the continent.

Foyle said that if the customer in question committed itself to a contract, Air Foyle would seek to lease an A300B4-200 freighter from one of two specialist U.S. Airbus leasing companies, Pinnacle Aircraft Leasing or C-S Aviation Services.
"I will know within the next three months whether or not this plan will go ahead," he said.
But Foyle stressed that this one-off project did not mean that Air Foyle would compete in the Airbus freighter market in any major form.
"The trouble is that there are now too many of these aircraft either already operating or on order," he noted.
"The A300 is a good aircraft and the only one of its type that is the right price, has Stage 3 (noise level accreditation) and offers 40 tonnes of payload volume," he said.

But he pointed out that Channel Express had already purchased two A300B4-200Fs (with a third planned), European consortium Farnair had contracted two and HeavyLift Cargo Airlines is to lease two more.
"So in the next 12 to 15 months, there will be about eight of these aircraft appearing in the market. How many airlines and integrators are there around to soak up all this extra capacity," he said.
Foyle added that integrator DHL it had recently announced it is to take three converted A300B4 freighters on long-term lease (from Pinnacle) and was therefore unlikely to be an additional customer.
